steps.text: Mix together peanut butter, butter or margarine, confectioners' sugar, and graham cracker crumbs. Shape into 1 inch balls and place in the freezer for 15 to 30 minutes, until firm.

Place chocolate and shortening in the top of a double boiler over simmering water. Stir frequently, scraping down the sides with a rubber spatula to avoid scorching, until chocolate is melted, about 5 minutes.

Remove peanut butter balls from the freezer and dip each ball into the chocolate mixture one at a time, using a toothpick to skewer the ball and cover all sides in chocolate. Remove ball from chocolate and place on a cookie sheet or tray lined with waxed paper. Repeat with remaining balls.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Peanut Butter Balls
raw_recipe.description: These chocolate peanut butter balls with graham crackers are also known as buckeyes. Make these balls of peanut butter coated in chocolate for your holiday cookie platter.

review.reviewBody:
These were great. After dipping, I sprinkled with pecans and coconut! Very easy. 
Tip: Put balls in freezer to firm before dipping. Makes it much easier

Every single time I make these everyone goes SO CRAZY!! No one wants Reese's Peanut Butter cups, they WANT THESE!! I do not use the shortening for the chocolate, and I do use Hershey's chocolate. I just put the chocolate into the microwave for 20 seconds, than 10 seconds at a time. until melted. Also I AM LAZY!!! LOL!! I put the mixture into a brownie pan, spread the chocolate over it. TA DA so much easier!! HINT for the cutting keep warming your knife in hot water after first letting it sit out at room temp for an hour.

Have been doing this for years will share a few tricks of mine. Some have it right put the mix in the freezer in a metal mixing bowl as it gets colder quicker for about 30 minutes. Double the recipe and the total amount of p. butter after doubling is 4 cups. Also use 1 bag of semi-sweet chips and 1 bag of milk chocolate chips and 3/4 bar of parafin wax. To cut your work way down and the overall key is I use a fondue pot as I got one as a gift specifically to make p. butter balls. The fondue pot comes with forks to dip with, and what helps overall the chocolate mixture stays warm to dip with. Hope this helps as I am sharing some major learnings acquired over the years! Not bragging, but it will be 5 stars now after the tips...just needed tweaking.

I made them just as the recipe directed and they were absolutely decadent. I found an excellent twist. I used brown sugar (1 cup) and three packets of Truvia, then doubled the graham crackers. I then used 1/8 teaspoon of salt to bring out the peanut taste. I recommend putting the graham crackers into a food processor to create a smooth texture. This way it is less sugar. Ghiradelli is perfect. I tried the 60% Cacao and it made the perfect cover. Also, I only dipped the balls half way to save on chocolate. Thanks for the awesome starter recipe, Sharon!
These are to die for! I made a couple of changes, used 3/4 c butter and 3 cups confection sugar. I also chilled the peanut butter mixture for about 1/2 hour before rolling them into balls. Enjoy!

I made these and they are delicious. After reading other reviews, I added some extra peanut butter, vanilla and the full powdered sugar. I also dusted my hands with the sugar to make rolling easy, used a small scoop and got around 90 piecesj, which I froze with tooth picks. Used a bag of semi-sweet and a bag of milk chocolate chips with the shortening, melted in a mini crock pot - worked great. I will definitely use this recipe again.

I was looking for a quick and easy recipe for my mom's christmas party and I came across this. I made just as the recipe said but didn't have semi-chocolate chips and had to use milk chocolate instead. I didn't think it would be such a hit but everyone loved these. People were grabbing whatever was left as I was walking out the door with them and ended up going home with only three left. A tip from another reviewer about putting them in the freezer for a little bit to make them more stiff so they would stick on a toothpick for dipping was very helpful. I also don't have a double boiler so I just heated the chocolate mixture over low heat.

We used 2 bags of Ghiradelli semi-sweet chocolate chips. We used a mellon baller to portion out the 120 dough balls. We also put them in the freezer before dipping them. We found small tongs were better for dipping them in the melted chocolate rather than tooth picks. They kept coming off the tooth picks and then were difficult to get back on. When they were all dipped, we put them on waxed paper in the refrigerator to harden the chocolate and decided to leave them there.

I gave this 4 stars because I did make some changes. First off I only used 3 cups of Confectioners sugar which in my opinion was more than enough as they were really sweet. I also used 1 sleeve of graham crackers which was all I had on hand and added powdered milk to the mix until the peanut butter mixture was the consistency I wanted. These were wonderful and I will definitely be making them again, though I may cut the sugar to 2 or 2-1/2 cups next time and just add more cracker crumbs and powdered milk so they aren't so sweet. I also recommend making them smaller than 1 inch as they are very rich.

Great Recipie! Simple to make. Easy to decorate. Yummy too!! 

As for the recipie itself you need more chocolate to coat than it calls for. Thankfully I had extra chocolate on hand to melt otherwise I wouldn't have had enough coat the balls. Using a toothpick to dip them and freezing them to firm up is The best thing for dipping them easily. I also liked the milk chocolate better with the peaunt butter. I wanted a little less sugar in these because I wasn't fond of it with all four cups so I added a 1/4 cup of Peanut Butter and 1/2 cup of crushed graham crackers. Still had an amazing texture. 

Also if you want to drizzle with peanut butter take chips and melt with shortening or Peanut butter to give a loose consitancy to drizzle over the balls. These are my new go to for gifts and any event.

I give the peanut butter mixture of this recipe a million and one stars because it's fantastic. The only snag I ran into was the chocolate. First problem - not enough. 2 cups only covers about 1/2, so double that for sure. Second problem - dunking. I took the advice of another reviewer and popped them in the freezer. This is definitely necessary and the toothpick in the center helps too. My problem was that I took them out of the freezer while I was melting my chocolate, so they warmed up again. Oops. Best to put the toothpick in, put them in the freezer to get almost hard, then dunk immediately. I plan to make these again and again, and hopefully find a way to perfect the dunking technique to reduce the inevitable mess. Thanks for a great recipe!

My family loves these so much. I’ve been making them every Christmas for a long time. I add some extra peanut butter, probably 1/2 cup. Instead of the chocolate chips and shortening, I use candy melts. They’re super easy to use and melt very smooth in the microwave.
Easy and fool proof. The family loved them.

These have a BETTER overall texture and Flavor than ones I have made in the past without the graham cracker addition These are as close to a Reeces cup as you can get The only difference between a peanut butter ball and Buckeye is less chocolate Lol Excellent recipe

They're delicious. My family loves them. But they are not Buckeyes. Real Buckeyes do not have graham crackers in them. No self-respecting "Buckeye" would put graham crackers in them and pass them off as Buckeyes.

I love the addition of graham cracker crumbs in this recipe. I halved the recipe (full recipe during the holidays). I needed to add a bit of additional shortening to get the chocolate as smooth as possible and also chilled the balls prior to dipping to be sure they held up. The next time I make them, I'll likely drizzle the remaining chocolate over the tops to make them look a bit fancier.
Adding 1/2 cup more of peanut butter and graham crackers.
Family favorite at Christmas
I stopped at 3 cups of powdered sugar. The mixture was sweet enough. Other than that, it was awesome!
I used about half the sugar, and I'm glad I did! they were awesome, and very addictive
